ThinkPad X1 Carbon

Light enough to forget.

A 14-inch OLED flagship that weighs under a kilogram, with the keyboard people still switch back for.

Weight & battery

Under one kilogram. All day.

Carbon-fibre and magnesium keep the chassis at about 0.98 kg, and a 57 Wh battery on an efficient Intel Core Ultra processor carries you through a workday.

0.98 kgStarting weight, 2.17 lb
14″2.8K OLED, 120 Hz, 100% DCI-P3
57 WhBattery with rapid charge
15.4 mmThin at its thickest point

Keyboard

The red dot stays.

Long-travel, concave keys and a TrackPoint nub in the middle let you point without leaving the home row. Forty years on, it is still the fastest way to select text.

1.5 mm key travel · spill-resistant design · backlit

Why people stay

Quiet details. Real work.

Durability

Tested past the spec sheet

Drops, dust, humidity, vibration and temperature extremes. It is tested against MIL-STD-810H methods.

Security

Locked from the chip up

Fingerprint reader in the power button, IR camera sign-in, a physical webcam shutter and a discrete security chip.

Connectivity

Wi-Fi 7 and Thunderbolt 4

Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1 and a headphone jack mean most docks and displays just work.

AI on device

An NPU that earns its place

Background blur, noise removal and live captions run on the neural processor, so the battery and fans barely notice.

Sound

Four speakers, four mics

Dolby Atmos speakers and a quad-mic array make long calls clear on both ends.

Linux ready

Runs what you run

Certified for Ubuntu and Fedora, with Windows 11 Pro available on every configuration.
